external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded supplier paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: Supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review it.

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: The service loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor platform where supplier compliance documents remain stored.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in the organisation's cloud account into which supplier records are written.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork and contact details through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the portal using credentials issued by the vendor.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.
data_flows.authentication: username and password issued by the vendor

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded supplier compliance paperwork and contact details.

data_flows.name: store paperwork
data_flows.description: The portal stores supplier documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance documents and contact details.

data_flows.name: retrieve paperwork
data_flows.description: The portal retrieves uploaded paperwork from the vendor platform for review.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.notes: The source states that uploaded documents remain in the vendor platform and are reviewed through the portal; the retrieval interaction is represented as the portal reading from that store.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded supplier compliance paperwork and contact details.

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: System description: "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." System description: "The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is." These claims conflict, so encryption in transit is unknown.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the supplier data extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes extracted supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract.

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-hosted environment for the SaaS portal and its platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's contents are confidential because it stores supplier compliance documents and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that supplier compliance paperwork and contact details remain in the vendor platform.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's contents are confidential because it receives a supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the landing bucket receives a supplier data extract containing supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's contents are confidential because it stores supplier records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
